lyrics:
[Intro: bright banjo-guitar riff, big drums]

[Verse 1: sunny male tenor]
Kids are at your mama's till tomorrow at noon
No car seats to buckle, no cartoon tunes
Baby, grab your sunglasses, leave the diaper bag
I gassed up the sweetest ride we ever had

[Pre-Chorus: rising melody, harmonies]
She's got sliding doors and a juice-box stain
And nineteen cupholders, and she's calling your name

[Chorus: huge, melodic, windows-down singalong]
Baby, it's a minivan with the windows down
Third row folded, we own this town
Turn up that song from our senior year
You still look seventeen from over here
She ain't fast, she ain't loud, she ain't new
But she's paid off, and I'm with you
Minivan with the windows down

[Verse 2: tenor, band bouncing]
There's cereal in the vents and a sock I can't explain
A sticker of a unicorn stuck on the windowpane
But you put your bare feet up and you let your hair come loose
And suddenly it's oh-four and I've borrowed Dad's coupe

[Pre-Chorus: rising melody, harmonies]
She's got sliding doors and a juice-box stain
And nineteen cupholders, and she's calling your name

[Chorus: huge, melodic, windows-down singalong]
Baby, it's a minivan with the windows down
Third row folded, we own this town
Turn up that song from our senior year
You still look seventeen from over here
She ain't fast, she ain't loud, she ain't new
But she's paid off, and I'm with you
Minivan with the windows down

[Bridge: half-time, handclaps, shouted]
(Hey!) Park it by the lake
(Hey!) For old times' sake
Automatic doors, baby, no mistake

[Final Chorus: loudest, gang vocals]
Baby, it's a minivan with the windows down
Third row folded, we own this town
Turn up that song from our senior year
You still look seventeen from over here
She ain't fast, she ain't loud, she ain't new
But she's paid off, and I'm with you
Minivan with the windows down

[Outro: riff, a door chime, spoken]
Did you remember the milk?
Tomorrow.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 148 BPM felt in half-time, 4/4, B-flat major. Loud, sunny and bouncing, a summer chorus with the roof off.

VOICE: Male tenor, bright and grinning, with a second voice in tight harmony above him throughout the pre-chorus and chorus. Gang shouts in the bridge. Two spoken lines at the end, hers first.

INSTRUMENTS: A bright riff played on banjo and electric guitar together, loud rock guitars in the chorus, a hip-hop style kick and snare, bass, handclaps, a little programmed percussion.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro riff. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:30 Pre-chorus. 0:40 Chorus 1. 1:08 Verse 2. 1:28 Pre-chorus. 1:38 Chorus 2. 2:06 Bridge, half-time shouts. 2:20 Final chorus. 2:50 Outro riff, a door chime and two spoken lines, ends 3:06.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2010s radio country: compressed, bright and huge, guitars and harmonies stacked wide.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The rising pre-chorus line about nineteen cupholders at 0:34.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a boy, a truck and a girl he has just noticed. This is the couple that song produced, two decades and several children later, still doing it.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Giddy, proud, seventeen again, back to real life with a grin.
